implementationScope: All 13 files changed by author fc5378b against 097522d: company CSV route, personal-tax service, native/role tests, CSV UI/client/helpers/tests and related documentation.
conclusions: The browser reads the actual generated Blob at the anchor download boundary, requires the fixed personal-tax-input.csv filename and exact numeric CRLF CSV, restores the patched anchor method in finally, and verifies the submitter has no download control. Native assertions require one export receipt for the preparer while preserving the prior creation/retry/read scenario.

The actual HTTP route uses the separate personal_tax.export permission, current unique active company membership and company-lock ordering. Only owners and personal-tax preparers are admitted; submitter read access does not confer export authority.

The service selects no taxpayer identifier and validates canonical company/record scope, integer year and exact bigint pence. It builds one fixed year/pence/GBP CSV row without free text, formulas, configurable fields or identifiers.

Protected storage/audit checks and the verified minimal export receipt commit precede attachment and scope headers or CSV bytes. Denials and audit failures return bounded JSON with no attachment metadata. A receipt describes an authorised prepared response, not proof that a browser saved or opened a file.

Express implicit HEAD is explicitly rejected with 405 and Allow GET before the service, producing no export receipt. Query overrides and malformed identities fail closed. res.end avoids automatic conditional 304/ETag behavior; a conditional GET is a fresh 200 response with its own receipt. All route responses are no-store.

Client export uses authenticated same-origin no-store GET, disallows redirects, validates the media type, fixed filename, company/record scope headers and exact bounded CSV against the loaded record, and reads no private denial/error bodies.

The keyed actor/company/role workspace and layout-effect cleanup cancel download generations on result removal/unmount. A stale transport response cannot create a Blob even if it ignores abort. 401/403 clears previous sensitive fields; temporary link and object URL are released. Documentation correctly explains that an already initiated download cannot be retracted and server audit may commit after cancellation.

Seven native scenarios cover role admission, exact bigint CSV and redacted receipts, SQL-level taxpayer exclusion, equal-ID company isolation, deny cases, HEAD/query/method/conditional behavior, revocation after lock wait, audit exception/silent suppression and unsafe storage/guard refusal. Fixture protections are restored in finally. No schema, calculation, posting or filing authority is added.
